# Startup readback: AI-44

Contract version: 1

## Objective and acceptance outcomes

Complete the canonical action lifecycle from proposal through deterministic policy, required approval, idempotent execution, truthful receipt, and supported reversal/closure. Acceptance: (1) risk, action type, authority channel, and capability determine the policy; agent proposals requiring approval cannot execute early, while a verified Gmail command fixture does not receive generic content classification or duplicate approval; (2) every execution checks current-state preconditions immediately before its side effect and replay returns the original effect/receipt; (3) timeout, rejection, cancellation, defer/partial result, prohibited action, and supported reversal leave persisted states and receipts that accurately represent what happened.

## Dependencies and relevant contracts

AI-13 (#167), AI-14 (#163), AI-15 (#165), and AI-19 (#171; shared integration rules #172) are Done. Relevant contracts are `packages/contracts/src/execution.ts` and its tests, `public.actions`, `public.approvals`, `public.execution_requests`, append-only `public.execution_receipts`, the `decide_approval()` RPC, authenticated Edge boundaries, and the AI-14/15 run and evidence records. Build Spec §§7.3–7.4, 13.2, 16.3 govern reauthentication, RLS, execution, and audit; Agent Spec §§1.2, 14.1, 25.9 and work-package F §32 distinguish verified command authority from agent proposal approval; Frontend Constitution §§15.1–15.3 governs approval context, action hierarchy, and execution receipts. AI-24/58 own real Gmail transport, so this ticket proves verified-command policy with a fixture. Integration contract: use authenticated Edge/RPC boundaries, owner-scoped data access, fresh AAL2 for web approval, persisted authority/channel and correlation, and append-only receipts; risks include EDGE-01, DB-05, DB-07/08, ACC-01/02, and OPS-01.

## Implementation and boundaries

Current schemas had bounded proposal/approval/queue states, owner-scoped request keys, append-only receipts, and an approval RPC, but no production action execution consumer. This lane adds the canonical execution store, atomic policy/claim/receipt RPCs, request-to-adapter dispatcher, and one bounded production adapter: promotion and reversal of an evaluated Systems `controlled-agent-report` prompt through `transition_prompt_version()`. The adapter checks the active version immediately before the side effect and uses an idempotency key; rollback verifies the promoted version and links its terminal receipt to the original receipt. Calendar/Reminders, worker, Gmail transport, and other connection side effects remain with their owning tickets. Policy is deterministic and independent of free text; agent proposals cannot borrow verified Gmail authority. Transactions, investments, purchases, and unsupported outreach remain denied before side effects. Preserve existing authentication, RLS, spending, action approval, and worker command boundaries. Do not modify unrelated shell, Career, Procurement, or worker areas.
